ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Higuchi Ichiyō Synthetic CCD — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

text.paragraph: New patient visit for seven weeks of cough, fevers, night sweats and weight loss: chest X-ray, sputum specimens, blood tests, airborne precautions, and a report of suspected tuberculosis to the public health center. Concerns: She has coughed for weeks, sweats at night and has lost weight, and fears it is tuberculosis; She supports her household by writing and cannot afford to stop working or to pay for many tests; She is afraid of passing the illness to the people she lives with and of what neighbors and editors will think. [S]

tr.td: New patient visit for seven weeks of cough, fevers, night sweats and weight loss: chest X-ray, sputum specimens, blood tests, airborne precautions, and a report of suspected tuberculosis to the public health center
Results visit: pulmonary tuberculosis confirmed; infectious diseases consultation and the start of the standard six-month regimen
Two-week review on treatment: culture result, liver tests, vision, and release from precautions
End of the eight-week intensive phase: susceptibility results, the two-month sputum culture, and the start of the continuation phase
Same-day sick visit for acute cystitis during tuberculosis treatment

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Diagnosis and safety: chest X-ray; three sputum specimens at least eight hours apart, one early in the morning, for acid-fast smear, Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra, liquid and solid culture and drug susceptibility testing; HIV, hepatitis B and hepatitis C tests and a pregnancy test; blood count, liver and kidney tests, glucose and hemoglobin A1c; visual acuity and color vision before ethambutol

Infectious diseases consultation at the results visit to confirm the diagnosis, choose between the six-month and four-month regimens, set the doses for her weight, and plan monitoring and infection control

Infection control and public health: airborne precautions in the clinic; at home, no visitors, a surgical mask in shared rooms, windows open, and sleeping in her own room until the public health center confirms she is no longer infectious; report of suspected tuberculosis to the public health center the same day and notification at once on diagnosis; a contact investigation of her household and other close contacts led by the public health center

Nutrition, income and writing: two dietitian visits in the first month, three meals and two energy-dense snacks a day with two oral nutrition supplement drinks, and weight at every visit; a medical social worker to apply for public funding of tuberculosis treatment and to review other help with costs; a paced writing plan of short sessions in daylight with rest; PHQ-9 at intake, at two months and at the end of treatment

Treatment: isoniazid 200 mg, rifampin 450 mg, pyrazinamide 1000 mg and ethambutol 600 mg daily for eight weeks, then isoniazid and rifampin daily for eighteen weeks, with pyridoxine 50 mg, by daily video-observed therapy with the public health center; ethambutol stopped once the isolate is susceptible to isoniazid and rifampin; liver tests at two weeks and monthly in the intensive phase because of her low weight and albumin; visual acuity and color vision monthly while on ethambutol; sputum smear and culture at two weeks and two months; chest X-ray at the end of treatment

Acute cystitis: nitrofurantoin 100 mg twice daily for five days with urine culture; no fluoroquinolone, because these drugs are kept for drug-resistant tuberculosis and can blur the picture of tuberculosis; continue every tuberculosis dose; plenty of fluids; return for fever, flank pain, vomiting or symptoms that are not better in two days

Prevention: cervical cytology now and every three years; Tdap; hepatitis B vaccine in two doses and HPV vaccine in three doses; influenza vaccine in the autumn; folic acid 0.4 mg daily advised; contraception counseling that rifampin makes hormonal pills, patches, rings and implants unreliable, with a copper IUD, injectable progestin or condoms as reliable choices if she needs contraception during treatment
Complete 182 daily doses within about six and a half months by video-observed therapy
All 182 doses completed in 26 weeks: 56 in the intensive phase and 126 in the continuation phase, none missed
Sputum culture negative at two months
The cultures taken at two weeks and at two months both showed no growth after six weeks
Weight at least 44 kg (BMI about 20) by the end of treatment
44.0 kg at the end of treatment, from 38.5 kg at intake
Keep writing on a paced schedule without losing income during treatment
Public funding covered most treatment costs; she kept writing about two hours a day and finished new work
No drug-induced liver injury or loss of vision during treatment
Liver tests normal throughout; visual acuity unchanged
